summary_paragraph: A woman with metastatic rectal adenocarcinoma and sickle cell disease was admitted for acute-on-chronic left lower extremity edema and left inguinal lymphadenopathy. She denied chest pain or shortness of breath but had mild pulmonary edema on imaging and elevated D-dimer, prompting admission for monitoring despite refusal of CT angiography. Doppler ultrasound and CT venogram ruled out deep vein thrombosis. She received a blood transfusion for symptomatic anemia, with labs indicating hemolysis from sickle cell disease. An MRI of the calf showed no osteosarcoma recurrence. A core biopsy of the left inguinal lymph node was performed to evaluate for cancer metastasis, with results pending at discharge. Her pain was managed with Dilaudid, and she remained stable throughout the hospitalization. She was discharged home with plans to follow up with her oncologist for biopsy results and ongoing management.
problems: Secondary and unspecified malignant neoplasm of inguinal and lower limb lymph nodes
